subject: Queueing curve, egress guardrails and VPC pool scaling decision
messages:
From: SRE Lead - Acme Corp <sre@acme.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: pm@acme.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Initial capacity ask: sustained qps vs tail latency constraints for VPC pool

Hi Hannah / Laura,

We’re finalizing procurement for the private VPC GPU pool and need to align on two hard constraints before we sign the purchase order:

1) Sustained throughput target: 15k embeddings/second (peak bursts to ~40k for short windows)
2) Tail latency SLA: P99 < 180ms for generation requests (90 tokens typical)

Our infra team is concerned about network egress caps (we have a multi-AZ setup) and about warm-up time when traffic shifts from hosted to private. Can you share a recommended admission control curve and any guardrails for egress budgeting?

Also copied PM so they can track timeline. We’d like a decision matrix by EOD Monday (9/13).

Thanks,
Alex Reyes
SRE Lead, Acme Corp

--
Attachment: none

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask: sustained qps vs tail latency constraints for VPC pool

Alex — thanks for the clarity. Short answers up front: we can meet the sustained throughput target with a mixed-pool strategy (primary high-memory GPUs + warm standby), and we recommend admission control to protect P99 by shedding or deferring low-value requests during bursts.

I’m attaching our quick runway calculator and a warmup curve illustration to help you validate headroom with the expected concurrency mix. Two asks from our side before we finalize the decision matrix:

- Can you share the expected per-request token distribution (median/95/99)?
- Is egress a hard cap per-AZ, or a pooled limit across your VPC?

Proposed short-term ops play: reserve a 25% warm pool (pre-warmed KV caches, active collectors) and tune admission-control threshold at 60% of sustained capacity to keep P99 headroom. Long-term: add dynamic spillover to hosted fallback for non-sensitive traffic.

Call to action: I’ll run a quick sim once you send the token distribution. Meeting if helpful — I can do 4–4:30pm PT today.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Alex — I put together a short table (see summary below) and a CSV with egress estimates attached. High-level assumptions: 90-token gen, 4 tokens/sec processing equivalence, KV cache hit 35% on steady-state.

Summary (provisional):
- Raw capacity per GPU type: A100-80GB -> ~3.2k embeddings/s or ~1.1k gen qps (90 tokens)
- Effective sustained capacity with 25% warm pool: ~2.4k embeddings/s per GPU equivalent
- For 15k sustained -> ~7 GPU equivalents + 2 for warm / buffer = 9 nodes (reserve 20% for failover)
- Admission control thresholds: soft reject at 65% sustained, hard reject at 90% sustained; queue depth target < 250ms average

Network/egress: attach egress_limits.csv with per-AZ suggested caps and conservative windowed bursting (max short burst per-AZ = +2.5x for 30s). If you have a pooled egress allowance we can smooth the same traffic across AZs.

Attachment: egress_limits.csv (text/csv, 12KB)

Jonas
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Hannah/Jonas — that helps. A couple of clarifying points:

- The 15k sustained target is per-customer VPC (single tenant), not pooled across customers.
- Our legal/compliance team will only allow fallback to hosted endpoints for non-PII flows; timeline for that is a hard requirement.
- We care most about P99 tail — P90 can be relaxed to 60–80ms.

Two asks: can you model an admission-control curve that prioritizes model-completion requests > 50 tokens, and produce a worst-case egress burn table for a 5-minute sustained burst? We want to feed that to our network team.

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>; Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>; SRE Lead - Acme Corp <sre@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 12:20:00 -0000
Subject: Decision proposal: admission policy + egress guardrails + staged deployment

Alex / team — based on the inputs, here’s a compact decision proposal for Acme’s VPC pool. The goal is to minimize operational churn and keep P99 < 180ms while respecting your compliance constraints.

1) Topline sizing: provision 11 GPU equivalents (A100-80GB class) across 3 AZs. Rationale: Jonas’ effective capacity numbers + 20% for failover and maintenance.

2) Warm pool & cache: reserve 3 nodes (~27%) as warm (KV preload + warmed CUDA kernels). Warm pool kept in active-standby so warmup time < 45s for ramp.

3) Admission control curve (token-prioritized):
   - Priority A: completion requests > 50 tokens -> allowed up to 75% sustained capacity
   - Priority B: short completions & embeddings -> allowed up to 55% sustained capacity; beyond that, Queueing admitted with best-effort and token-drop policy
   - Hard cutoff: > 95% sustained capacity -> reject non-critical requests (503 + retry-after)

4) Egress guardrails:
   - Default per-AZ pooled cap: 1.2 Gbps sustained, allow 2.8 Gbps for 45s burst window with token-bucket smoothing
   - If per-AZ hard cap lower than 1 Gbps, redistribute load across AZs via router policy and activate spillover to private warm standby in another region (needs config)

5) Fallback and telemetry:
   - Hosted fallback allowed for non-PII only; tag traffic via header to enforce policy.
   - Implement a rolling canary: 10% traffic for 48h -> 50% for 24h -> full cutover.

6) Operational runbook highlights:
   - Pre-warm triggers: when 5-min moving average > 60% for 2 consecutive windows, spin up 1 warm node.
   - Alerts: P99 > 160ms for 10m -> page oncall and start controlled throttle at 70% sustained.

I attached a short PDF with the decision rationale and the admission-control curve graphic for your network team. If this looks good, we’ll update the infra playbook and create the INF Jira tickets for provisioning.

Irene Choi
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: decision-proposal-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 92KB)

Alex — thanks for the quick turn. All looks actionable; confirm the following as our shared decision and next steps: 

- Provisioning: 11 A100-equivalent GPU nodes across 3 AZs; 3-node warm pool. (INF-4982 created for infra team)
- Admission policy: implement Irene’s token-priority curve; Jonas to produce the exact token-threshold YAML for infra coders by COB Monday.
- Egress: Acme to confirm if egress allowance is pooled; if pooled we’ll apply the 1.2 Gbps sustained / 2.8 Gbps 45s burst policy; otherwise we’ll distribute via AZ router rules.
- Compliance: hosted fallback flagged as non-PII only (PM to provide list of non-PII flows).
- Runbook: Vivek to author the ~2-page oncall runbook highlighting warmup triggers and throttling thresholds.

Can we lock a 30-minute handoff call Monday 9/13 16:00 PT to finalize the token distribution and hand off INF tickets? I’ll send invites once you confirm.

Thanks everyone — we’ll attach these decisions to the Drive folder and move to provisioning after Acme signs the PO.

Hannah Schmitt
